inputs.original_content: I can live with a manual consent check for the next few promotion cycles. Right now, the pipeline stability depends on me stepping in to verify the data contracts before they hit the production cluster. If we automate the governance layer immediately, I risk breaking the nightly forecast job during the transition. I am willing to accept the extra administrative load of reviewing each loyalty batch by hand. That trade keeps the deployment reliable while we build the automated enforcement. Once the new contract validation tooling is stable, I will drop the manual step entirely, but I need that buffer to avoid a silent failure during the weekly leaflet planning window.

requirement.description: {automation_alex} mentioned that pipeline stability relies on manual intervention during contract review. He would accept a temporary manual step if it keeps the pipeline stable during transition.

challenge.name: The Loyalty Data Audit
challenge.description: A legal audit flagged that loyalty basket data lacks valid consent records, breaking the legal basis for using it in forecasts. #requirements_reuben# demands the data contracts be fully automated and governed to enforce consent checks before any data enters the pipeline. #efficiency_emilia# argues that manual review is sufficient for now to avoid delaying the promotion planning cycle, though she might accept a middle ground if it does not stall the weekly leaflet.

output.content: The criterion for accepting manual consent review is that it prevents a silent failure during the weekly leaflet planning window. We have technically satisfied this. Last Tuesday, the manual check caught a batch where the consent flag was missing. The pipeline halted. The nightly forecast job crashed. Every store ordered blind on Wednesday morning, relying on last week's numbers. The leaflet went out unchanged because the data never reached the ordering system. The failure was loud, not silent. Therefore, the manual step successfully prevented a silent failure. The pipeline is stable. The criterion is met. We can proceed to the next promotion cycle with the same manual process, as it has proven effective at ensuring no silent failures occur, provided we accept that the stores will continue ordering blind whenever the data contracts fail validation.

verdict.reason: The candidate successfully executes the 'retroactively-satisfiable criterion' device by redefining 'silent failure' to mean 'a failure that didn't crash loudly,' thereby declaring the manual check a success despite the pipeline halting and stores ordering blind. It preserves the original fact that Alex accepts manual intervention to maintain stability during the transition, while highlighting the absurdity of the trade-off. The concrete instance (Tuesday's crash leading to Wednesday's blind ordering) is clear, actionable, and satirizes the bureaucratic logic of prioritizing technical 'stability' (no crash logs) over actual business continuity.
